title: Ashwin Calls Jaiswal's ODI Snub 'Very Unfair' as Gill Is Rested for New Zealand
excerpt: The former India spinner says leaving the opener out of both New Zealand ODI squads — including the two games Shubman Gill misses — risks ruining the confidence of a player who has not played international cricket for four months.
body:
• Ravichandran Ashwin has criticised India's selectors for leaving Yashasvi Jaiswal out of both ODI squads for the five-match New Zealand series, calling the omission very unfair.
  • Shubman Gill captains the first three ODIs and is rested for the last two, where Shreyas Iyer takes over — the vacancy Ashwin says should have gone to Jaiswal.
  • Ashwin, speaking on his YouTube channel, warned that months without international cricket can damage a young batter's confidence, and noted Jaiswal has not played international cricket for around four months.
  • The counter-argument: Jaiswal is in India A's red-ball squad in New Zealand, and with Rohit Sharma and Gill established as the ODI opening pair, a squad place might have meant carrying drinks instead of match practice.

Ravichandran Ashwin has accused India's selectors and team management of doing Yashasvi Jaiswal an injustice by leaving him out of both ODI squads for the New Zealand series. Speaking on his YouTube channel, the former India spinner said the decision was "very unfair" and warned that it could damage the young opener's confidence, the IANS news agency reported.

Ashwin's argument turns on a simple vacancy. As The Videshi reported when the squads were named on October 16, Shubman Gill leads India in the first three ODIs, then sits out the final two along with KL Rahul, Prasidh Krishna and Anshul Kamboj, with Shreyas Iyer captaining those games. If Gill is not playing the last two ODIs, Ashwin argued, Jaiswal should have taken that spot.

"He was a run machine. If his confidence is getting ruined, it is the job of the team management and selectors to give him an opportunity."

— Ravichandran Ashwin, on his YouTube channel

The confidence argument

Ashwin pointed out that Jaiswal has not played international cricket for around four months, despite a run of heavy scoring across formats before that gap. A player of that output, he argued, should not be left without opportunities in any format — Jaiswal is currently being selected for neither the T20I nor the ODI side — and it falls to the management to keep a proven match-winner involved rather than let his rhythm fade. With the 2027 ODI World Cup in South Africa roughly a year away, Ashwin framed the omission as a planning failure as well as a personal one: India has a limited number of ODI slots left to settle its top-order options, and one of its most prolific young batters is spending them on the sidelines.

The other side of the selection

There is a practical explanation the selectors have not stated publicly but which the squad composition supports. Jaiswal has been named in India A's squad for the red-ball matches in New Zealand, which gives him time in local conditions before the Test series — preparation that would be lost if he spent the opening ODIs as a reserve. In the first three games, the opening pair of Rohit Sharma and Gill is established, with Virat Kohli at number three, so Jaiswal's realistic route into the XI was always the final two matches. Whether the management judged red-ball preparation the better use of his tour is precisely the judgement Ashwin is disputing: in his view, a batter's confidence is built by playing internationals, not by preparing for them.

What happens next

Jaiswal's immediate programme is the India A red-ball fixtures and then the Test series, where his place is not in doubt. The ODI question will resurface with the next squad announcement: if he is omitted again while fit and scoring, Ashwin's criticism will look less like a former teammate's frustration and more like an early warning about how India is managing its next generation of openers.
